subject: Follow-up: security posture, subprocessor boundaries & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Lehman <ari.lehman@finprospect.com>, procurement@finprospect.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: security posture, subprocessor boundaries & next steps

Hi Ari / team —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our demo + security portion and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

1) High-level posture
- We discussed Redwood's SOC 2 Type II timeline (in-scope controls completed; final attestation expected Q1 2027).
- GDPR data residency options: hosted (multi-region) vs Private (VPC) were reviewed; you expressed a tilt toward hosted with strict routing to us-east for primary data.
- No PHI expected for this pilot — but you asked about HIPAA readiness for future scope.

2) Subprocessors & boundaries (items you requested)
- Initial subprocessor list that covers cloud infra and analytics (we flagged primary cloud providers and telemetry vendors).
- Data sharing: inference requests do not persist full PII; we described prefix/KV caching policies and retention controls.

3) Actionables & who owns
- Redwoods: Share canonical subprocessor CSV and initiate vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) package (deliver by Monday EOD). — Marcus (owner)
- FinProspect: Send the security questionnaire (if you have a template) or confirm the VSQ receipt and any priority controls (encryption at rest, customer-managed KMS). — Ari
- Redwoods Security Ops: Pull more precise data flow diagram for inference path (including optional exporter services). — Grace

Attachments I'll send with the follow-up: redwood_subprocessors_list_v1.csv (mapping to roles), and an initial VSQ payload (RDW_VSQ_initial.zip) with SOC 2 scope summary and our encryption/retention FAQ.

Next steps: I'll upload artifacts to the shared Drive and ping the HubSpot record. Can we target Monday 11/23 for a short sync (15–20m) once you've reviewed the subprocessor list?

Thanks — talk soon.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_list_v1.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: RDW_VSQ_initial.zip (ZIP)]

From: Ari Lehman <ari.lehman@finprospect.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finprospect.com, Lucia Gomez <lgomez@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: security posture, subprocessor boundaries & next steps

Thanks Marcus — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2 timing: Q1 attestation window is fine; for procurement we need a current SOC 2 bridge letter or SOC 2 Interim report if available while you complete Type II. Do you have a current bridge doc?
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS for production; for pilot, Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable if we can restrict region to us-east. Can you confirm support?
- Subprocessors: Lucía (cc'd) will review your subprocessor CSV in detail. If you can call out any subprocessors that have cross-region storage (even transient), flag them.

We do have a short security questionnaire template; we'll send that once we receive your VSQ payload. Monday 11/23 works for a quick follow.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Ari
Head of Security Operations, FinProspect

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Lehman <ari.lehman@finprospect.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lucia Gomez <lgomez@cloudpartner.io>, procurement@finprospect.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: security posture, subprocessor boundaries & next steps

Ari — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and what's attached now: 

- Bridge letter: we do have a current SOC 2 bridge statement that summarizes control status and recent testing; included in RDW_VSQ_initial.zip (file: SOC2_bridge_statement_202610.pdf).
- KMS: pilot option — Redwood-managed keys can be restricted to us-east; production recommendation is to switch to customer-managed KMS (we list supported providers in the VSQ).
- Cross-region subprocessors: the CSV includes a "regions" column; flagged entries that may replicate logs/metrics outside us-east are marked with "(replicates)".

I uploaded both files to the shared Drive and attached a trimmed subprocessor CSV here for quick review. If Lucía wants, Grace can hop on a 15-minute call to walk dataflow and caching boundaries Monday before the sync.

Proposed tentative sync: Mon 2026-11-23 10:00am PT (30m) — I'll send a calendar invite after we hear back.

Marcus
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_list_v1.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: RDW_VSQ_initial.zip (ZIP)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Lehman <ari.lehman@finprospect.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@finprospect.com, Lucia Gomez <lgomez@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: security posture, subprocessor boundaries & next steps

Hi all — quick note from Security Ops:

Thanks for the review notes, Ari. A few clarifications before the call: 

- Bridge/interim docs: we confirm SOC2_bridge_statement_202610.pdf is the most current interim artifact. We will follow up with the auditor contact info if you need direct verification.
- KMS behavior: during pilot we can scope to Redwood-managed keys restricted to us-east and document how key rotation and access controls work; for production we will outline steps to integrate customer KMS (we support AWS KMS + external HSM via KMIP).
- Dataflow diagram: attached is a concise diagram that highlights inference request path, caching points, and where telemetry is collected. Note the telemetry collector aggregates anonymized metrics and does not capture full request bodies by default — customers can opt-out.

I've attached the diagram (RDW_inference_dataflow_v1.pdf) to the Drive link Marcus shared; will post a short note to the HubSpot record with the artifact references.

See you on the call if scheduled.

Grace O'Connor
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW_inference_dataflow_v1.pdf (PDF)]
